texts.facts: The present claim petition arises out of road accident that occurred on 18.01.2020, in which one Usha (aged about 40 years) allegedly suffered grievous injury. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 18.01.2020 at 7:30 a.m. victim Usha along with her friends Ruby, Priti, Seema, Priyanka, Pinki Devi and their minor children namely Adarsh@Arjun, Kapil, Radhika and Shahil were returning to Delhi from Aligarh after attending a marriage function. All of them were travelling in an Ecco car bearing no.DL-3CCR-1409, which was being driven by one Bhoop Singh. When they reached Chand Hut chowk, Palwal, a truck bearing no.HR-55G-7560 (hereinafter referred as to the offending vehicle), came in a rash and negligent manner and hit the Ecco Car. Due to the impact, all the passengers, including the driver, sustained severe injuries. All victims including Usha, were rushed to Civil hospital at Palwal from where she was referred to AIIMS Trauma center. Her MLC was prepared. 3. An FIR No.0018/2020, dated 18.01.2020, u/s 279/304-A/337 IPC was registered at PS Chand Hut, District Palwal. Police investigated the matter and filed a chargesheet u/s 279/337/338/304A IPC before concerned criminal court. Present claim petition has been filed in respect of injured Usha while separate claim petitions were filed before this Tribunal for compensation claim in respect of victim Ruby vide case titled as Ashutosh Dixit vs. Sant Prakash, MACT no.225/20, victim Charu by Charu gupta gupta 2025.12.17 17:26:43 +0530 MACT No:125/21 Usha vs.Sant Prakash & ors. P.No. 2 of 24 BK Seema vide case titled as Seema Devi vs. Sant Prakash, MACT no.119/21, victim Priti vide case titled as Priti vs. Sant Prakash, MACT no.123/21, Priyanka vide case titled as Priyanka Devi v. Sant Prakash, MACT no.121/21, minor Adarsh @ Arjun through his mother Priti vide case titled as Adarsh vs. Sant Prakash, MACT no.124/21,minor Gurpreet (since deceased) vide case titled as Priti vs. Sant Prakash, MACT no.118/21, minor Sahil (since deceased) vide case titled as Seema Devi v. Sant Pakash, MACT no.122/21 and Bhoop Singh, vide case titled as Bhoop Singh v. Sant Pakash, MACT no.120/21. 4. As per record, the offending vehicle was driven by respondent no.1, owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no. 3. 5. In response to the claim petition, respondent no.1 and 2 filed their written statement/reply without denying the occurrence of the accident, involvement of the offending vehicle or allegations or rash and negligent driving. It has been pleaded that Respondent no.1/driver of the offending vehicle possessed a valid driving licence at the time of accident, that the vehicle was duly insured, that the vehicle was fit to ply on the road and had requisite fitness and permit issued vide Form No.47, NPPUC. A written statement/reply was filed by respondent no.3 denying its liability to compensate the petitioner in case respondent no.1 and 2 were found to be in breach of the terms of the insurance policy. Insurance company has further raised a plea of contributory negligence on the part of victims in as much the Ecco Car was being plied in violation of the permit, beyond its seating capacity of 7 persons. It is pleaded that the Ecco car Charu by Charu gupta MACT No:125/21 Usha vs.Sant Prakash & ors. gupta 2025.12.17 Usha vs Sant Prakash on 17 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161270576/ 2 P.No. 3 of 24 BK 17:26:49 +0530 admittedly carried 12 passengers including the driver and must have met the accident owing to disbalance. 6. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 19.02.2022. 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 18.01.2020 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. HR-55G-7560 being driven by R1, owned by R2 and insured with R3? OPP 2. OPP. 3. Relief. 7. In order to prove her claim, petitioner/injured examined herself as PW-1. To prove her claim, petitioner /Usha led evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A wherein she deposed that on 08.01.2020 at about 7:30 a.m. injured was coming to her home from Aligarh, U.P after attending a marriage function by an Ecco car bearing no.DL3CCR1409 along with Seema, Priti, Priyanka, Piniki Devi and children namely Arjun, Kapil, Radhika and Shahil. When they reached at Chand Hut chowk at village Chandhut Palwal, Haryana, a vehicle bearing no.HR-55G-7560, came from opposite directions in a rash and negligent manner and hit the Ecco car. Due to sudden and forceful impact, injured sustained several grievous injuries. Victim was moved to Civil Hospital, Palwal, Haryana. where doctors referred her to Safdarjung Hospital. She was medically examined. She relied upon her Adhar Card as Ex.PW1/1, MLC as Ex.PW1/2, discharge summary as Ex.PW1/3, OPD and medical Charu Digitally signed by Charu gupta Date: 2025.12.17 gupta 17:26:55 +0530 MACT No:125/21 Usha vs.Sant Prakash & ors. P.No. 4 of 24 BK treatment as Ex.PW1/4, Medical bills and records as Ex.PW1/5 and DAR i.e. FIR, chargesheet, arrest memo, site plan, mechanical inspection as Ex.PW1/6. PW-1 was cross examined by all respondents. Ms. Priyanka/PW-2 was examined as an eye witness. She tendered her evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. She deposed that she was witness in all the 9 cases and injured in case titled as Priyanka vs. Sant Prakash. She relied upon her Adhar card as Ex.PW1/1, copy of her MLC as Ex.PW1/2, her OPD card as Ex.PW1/3, her medical bills as Ex.PW1/4 and complete criminal record as Ex.PW1/5. She was cross examined by learned counsel for insurance company and the same was adopted by Respondents did not lead any evidence despite opportunity. In this case, claimant has filed medical bills of Rs.7589/-. Insurance company is hereby directed to deposit the award amount in favour of the petitioner with State Bank of India, District Court Complex, Saket Court Branch, New Delhi by way of RTGS/NEFT/IMPS in account of MACT PARKING FUND, A/c No. 00000042706875094, IFS Code SBIN0014244 and MICR code 110002342 under intimation to the Nazir along with calculation of interest and to the Counsel for the petitioner.

However, before such traffic violation can be equated to contributory negligence, the concept of contributory negligence may be analysed through the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Usha vs Sant Prakash on 17 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161270576/ 4 Pramod kumar Rasikbhai Jhaveri Vs. Karmasey Kungvargi Tak and Ors.,C.A. No.5436 of 1994 decided on 05.08.2002, wherein it has been held as under: "...9. Subject to non-requirement of the existence of duty, the question of contributory negligence is to be decided on the same principle on which the question of defendant's negligence is decided. The standard of reasonable man is as relevant in the case of plaintiff's contributory negligence as in the case of defendant's negligence. The following observation of the High Court of Australia in Astley v. Austrust Ltd.1 is worthy of quoting: "A finding of contributory negligence turns on a factual investi-gation whether the plaintiff contributed to his or her own loss by failing to take reasonable care of his or her person or property. What is reasonable care depends on the circumstances of the case. In many cases, it may be proper for a plaintiff to rely on the defendant to perform its duty. But there is no abso-lute rule. The duties and responsibilities of the defendant are a variable factor in determining whether contributory negligence exists and, if so , to what degree. In some cases, the nature of the duty owed may exculpate the plaintiff from a claim of con-tributory negligence; in other cases, the nature of Charu by Charu gupta gupta 2025.12.17 17:27:11 +0530 MACT No:125/21 Usha vs.Sant Prakash & ors. P.No. 7 of 24 BK the duty may reduce the plaintiffs share of responsibility for the damage suffered; and in yet other cases the nature of the duty may not prevent a finding that the plaintiff failed to take reasonable care for the safety of his or her person or property. Contribu-tory negligence focuses on the conduct of the plaintiff. The duty owed by the defendant, although relevant, is one only of many factors that must be weighed in determining whether the plaintiff has so conducted itself that it failed to take reasonable care for the safety of its person or property." 13. Reliance also placed on recent decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mohd. Siddiqui vs. National Insurance Co. (2020) 3SCC 57 wherein the court while considering an issue of triple riding made following observations: " a pillion rider, even if accompanied by more than legally permitted number of passengers, does not automatically imply contributory negligence. For such a finding, it must be demonstrated that the pillion rider's action directly contributed to the occurrence of the accident or exacerbated its impact. The court emphasised that a violation of traffic laws such as exceeding the permissible number of riders on a motorcycle, does not by itself establish contributory negligence. There must be a clear causal connection between the violation and the accident". 14. Drawing an analogy from these decisions, in the present case, no causal connection or nexus between the overloading of Ecco car and the accident has been established by any of the Usha vs Sant Prakash on 17 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161270576/ 5 respondents. gupta 2025.12.17 17:27:17 +0530 MACT No:125/21 Usha vs.Sant Prakash & ors. P.No. 8 of 24 BK As such, no contributory negligence is liable to be deducted in the prevailing circumstances of the case. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 16. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam Insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. Now as regards the issue of quantum of compensation, this court relies upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC wherein it has been observed that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure; (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising; (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability; (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 20.1. 20.6. It was observed by Apex Court in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability --Item (ii) (a). 20.7.
